ai_show_review.summary: Blistering Smokestack Lightnin' into King Bee with raw 1967 board
ai_show_review.blurb: A tight two‑song blues jam that showcases Pigpen’s harp fury and Jerry Garcia’s sweet early‑era guitar tone. The soundboard capture is surprisingly clear for 1967, though crowd noise and occasional tape artifacts are audible. Overall a solid snapshot of the Dead’s raw pre‑psychedelic power.
ai_show_review.review: On February 12, 1967 at San Francisco’s Fillmore Auditorium the Grateful Dead delivered a concise but ferocious blues set that has become a prized artifact for early‑Dead collectors. The band launched straight into a scorching “Smokestack Lightnin'” before slipping seamlessly into “King Bee,” letting Ron "Pigpen" McKernan dominate with his harmonica and vocal grit while Jerry Garcia’s guitar floated sweet, crystalline tones that hint at the melodic sensibility to come. Bob Weir’s rhythm work holds steady through the five‑minute stretch, and Bill Kreutzmann provides a solid, no‑frills backbeat. Recorded from the house board by TheOtherWayne, the tape sounds remarkably good for its era—capturing the raw energy of the room with enough clarity to hear each instrument, even if occasional over‑saturation and digital modulation artifacts bite through the mix. For fans of the Dead’s formative blues period, this is arguably the best listening window into their early sound.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard from 1967 that captures the full blues jam with clear instrument separation, despite minor tape artifacts.
